Suresh: Heads-up — eu-central-1d region bring-up scheduled Tue 09:00 UTC. We need a concise soak+load runbook focused on autoscaler tuning, validation steps, and the handoff to oncall. Who can own the play and the post-run report?

Anya: I can draft the runbook. Quick sketch: provisioning smoke, controlled ramp, 24-48h soak, scale-stress, validation checks, and rollback criteria. Want concrete commands + Prom queries.

Lucas: I’ll take monitoring/alerts during the run. Can you include exact PromQL and dashboards to snapshot? I’ll pair with OpsBot to post alerts to #incidents.

Suresh: Perfect. Maria — can you own rollback and provider capacity ops if AZ imbalance shows up?

Maria: Yep. I’ll prepare the provider console play (how to drain, reprovision, and emergency scale). Also prep the quota request template.

Anya: Runbook outline (short):
- PREP: confirm nodepool sizing, GPU SKU (A100-40GB), cloud quotas, subnet/policy, service endpoints.
- SMOKE (15-30m): basic pod scheduling + single-gen request to validate model pinned version.
- RAMP (4h window): increase QPS to target baseline (1x) then to 2x, watch batching and queue depth.
- SOAK (24–48h): sustain baseline traffic patterns; include diurnal variation.
- STRESS: brief 1h 3x traffic spike to validate autoscaler ceilings and fallback.
- POST: collect snapshots, open incident if regressions, handoff doc.

Anya: Key autoscaler tuning knobs we should verify:
- cluster autoscaler min/max GPU nodes per AZ
- pod resource requests (gpu-count, mem, cpu) and headroom for kubelet eviction
- batching target size and batch timeout impacting GPU utilization
- queue-depth threshold that triggers scale-up (in our queue-watcher controller)

Anya: Example HPA-ish config we’ll test (K8s-like simplified):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-gpu-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 24
  metrics:
    - type: Pods
      pods:
        metric:
          name: gpu_utilization
        target:
          averageValue: 60
```

Anya: Example cluster-autoscaler nodepool settings (cloud CLI):
```bash
# set GPU nodepool min/max
cloudctl nodepool update --name=eu-gpu-pool --min-size=2 --max-size=40 --gpu-type=a100-40
```

Lucas: PromQL snippets I’ll wire to the dashboard:
- GPU utilization (per node): avg by (instance) (rate(gpu_utilization_percent[5m]))
- Batch size distribution: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Queue depth: sum(queue_depth)
- Inference latency p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Token generation rate: sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m]))

Lucas: Alerts to enable for the run:
- queue_depth > 500 for >5m -> paging (possible underprovision)
- p99 latency > 2s for >10m -> pager (degraded SLO)
- GPU_utilization > 90% for >10m -> notify (#eng-platform) (risk of hotspot)
- GPU_utilization < 20% sustained while pending pods exist -> autoscaler stuck

Suresh: SLO/thresholds for this region: target p50 < 120ms; p95 < 400ms at baseline. During stress tests accept p99 spikes. Cost guardrails: alert if cost-per-token > 2x expected for >1h.

Anya: Load generator commands (use our load image):
```bash
kubectl run loadgen --image=redwood/loadtest:stable --replicas=3 --env="TARGET=https://eu-central-1d-api.redwood.example"
# quick curl single request
curl -s -X POST 'https://eu-central-1d-api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```

Anya: Ramp plan details:
- 00:00–00:30 smoke: 5rps, single worker, confirm model loads and KV cache warms.
- 00:30–04:30 ramp: increase to baseline over 30m, hold each step 20m. baseline = expected prod QPS for region.
- 04:30–52:30 soak: sustain baseline, hold diurnal patch at +10% for 2 windows.
- 52:30–53:30 stress: 3x spike for 1h.

Maria: Provider notes — common network/placement issues:
- If controller shows pods Pending with "Insufficient GPUs", check AZ quotas and taints. Fix: expand nodepool per AZ or rebalance using podTopologySpread.
- If scheduling is uneven (one AZ hot), use immediate: cordon + drain non-essential GPU nodes in hot AZ, scale up under-utilized AZ nodepools.
- Emergency provider CLI commands (example):
```bash
# scale a specific nodepool fast
cloudctl nodepool scale --name=eu-gpu-pool-1 --replicas=10
# drain and reprovision a misbehaving node
cloudctl node drain --name=node-01 && cloudctl node delete --name=node-01
```

OpsBot: Reminder scheduled: Runbook owner: Anya. Monitoring lead: Lucas. Provider ops: Maria. Run start: 1769540000 (Tue 09:00 UTC). OpsBot will post start/stop in #incidents and create ephemeral channel. :robot_face:

Lucas: During run, I’ll snapshot dashboards every 30m and post to the ephemeral channel. I’ll also capture distributions of batch sizes — those are the most sensitive to latency/cost tradeoffs.

Suresh: Handoff expectations after run:
- CSV of key metrics (GPU_util, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, batch_size distribution)
- List of tuning changes applied with git hash for infra manifests
- Incident if any pager fired + RCA draft within 24h
- Cost delta estimate vs baseline

Maria: I’ll prepare the quota request template and the emergency escalation list for cloud support; linking both in the runbook doc.

Anya: I’ll push the runbook draft to docs/runbooks/region-bringup/ and include checklist + commands + templated dashboards. After the run I’ll update with actual graphs and a short TL;DR.

Suresh: Great. Action items: Anya — runbook + preflight checklist. Lucas — dashboards + alerts enabled. Maria — quota + emergency ops ready. OpsBot — create ephemeral channel and calendar invite. Everyone mark availability for Tue 09:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

Suresh: Thanks all — we’ll iterate on thresholds after the first soak. If we see persistent low GPU utilization with long queues, priority is tuning batch timeout before adding nodes.
